items.title: Rocket Lab wins NASA award for three Electron launches
items.summary: NASA has selected Rocket Lab to launch a pair of science missions on three Electron rockets in 2027. The post Rocket Lab wins NASA award for three Electron launches appeared first on SpaceNews .

items.title: Stanford Scientists Regrow Lost Cartilage and Reverse Arthritis in Major Breakthrough
items.summary: Stanford Medicine researchers achieved a groundbreaking treatment that blocks an aging-related protein, successfully restoring lost cartilage in old mice and helping prevent arthritis after knee injuries. Human cartilage samples showed similar signs of regeneration, raising hopes for future drugs that could replace joint surgery. The therapy dramatically improved movement and joint function by targeting the 15-PGDH protein linked to aging.

items.title: Prometheus AI Company Raises $12 Billion for Artificial General Engineers
items.summary: Biotech AI startup Prometheus secured a massive $12 billion funding round to develop artificial general engineers that can automate complex engineering tasks in drug discovery and biotechnology. The company aims to create AI systems capable of independent scientific reasoning and experimental design, potentially revolutionizing pharmaceutical research and development timelines.

items.title: Giant Underground Neutrino Detector Achieves Precision Breakthrough in China
items.summary: The massive JUNO neutrino observatory deep beneath the ground in China delivered its first major scientific breakthrough, achieving one of the most precise measurements yet of how elusive neutrino particles behave. This advancement brings scientists closer to cracking fundamental mysteries about neutrinos and could revolutionize our understanding of particle physics and the universe.

items.title: NASA Announces Artemis III Crew for Critical Moon Mission Testing
items.summary: NASA revealed the four-astronaut crew selected for the crucial Artemis III mission, designed to test rendezvous and docking procedures with lunar landers in Earth orbit next year. The mission represents a critical milestone before sending astronauts back to the Moon for landing in 2028, involving both SpaceX Starship and Blue Origin's Blue Moon Mark 2 landers.

items.title: Brain-Inspired Chip Functions Near Absolute Zero for Quantum Computing
items.summary: Scientists at the University of Hong Kong created a remarkable brain-inspired chip that can function just above absolute zero temperature, representing one of the coldest operational environments ever achieved. This breakthrough could transform quantum computing by enabling ultra-efficient processing in cryogenic conditions, potentially solving major energy challenges in quantum systems.

items.title: Scientists Discover Hidden Cause of Aging Cells That Can Be Reversed
items.summary: Researchers discovered that declining levels of phosphatidylcholine may be a major cause of age-related mitochondrial dysfunction and loss of cellular energy. Remarkably, boosting this nutrient restored more youthful mitochondrial performance in aging organisms, suggesting some aspects of aging can be slowed or reversed. This breakthrough from the Leibniz Institute on Aging offers hope for developing treatments to slow cellular aging processes.

items.title: Battery-Free Device Turns Sunlight Into Fuel Using Self-Regulating System
items.summary: Scientists have developed an artificial photosynthesis system that essentially regulates itself, eliminating the need for batteries used in many current designs. The key innovation is an electrolyzer that automatically adapts to changing sunlight by altering its electrical properties as it heats up. This keeps solar fuel production more stable while reducing cost and complexity. The system produces formic acid from carbon dioxide and water.

items.title: Revolutionary AI Cuts Robot Energy Use by 100x While Boosting Accuracy
items.summary: Researchers at Tufts University developed a neuro-symbolic AI system that combines neural networks with human-like symbolic reasoning, slashing energy consumption by up to 100 times compared to conventional approaches while dramatically improving performance. In robotic task tests using the Tower of Hanoi puzzle, the hybrid system achieved a 95% success rate versus 34% for standard models and trained in just 34 minutes versus more than a day and a half for traditional systems.

items.title: NASA's Next-Gen AI Space Chip Could Let Spacecraft Think for Themselves
items.summary: NASA is testing a next-generation space computer chip that could give spacecraft the ability to operate far more independently in deep space. With onboard artificial intelligence, spacecraft could respond to unexpected situations in real time when communication delays make human control impractical. The chip could also help deep space missions process, store, and transmit massive amounts of scientific data back to Earth more efficiently. The radiation-hardened processor shows performance levels hundreds of times beyond current spaceflight technology.

items.title: Scientists Reverse Anxiety by Fixing Tiny Brain Circuit in Breakthrough Study
items.summary: A newly identified group of amygdala neurons appears to play a central role in anxiety and social behavior. Restoring normal activity in this tiny brain circuit reversed anxiety and social deficits in mice, revealing a promising new target for treating anxiety disorders. The research offers hope for developing more targeted treatments for anxiety and social behavioral disorders by focusing on specific neural circuits rather than broad brain regions.
